that model is perfect. Need two models: one fully AI, one with more human interaction — people won't be ready for straight AI.
Throw in the model where the receiving interventionalist joins the line and the AI just connects the two.

v0.23: physician-to-physician is the default at enrollment; AI connects the ER physician to the interventionalist (or shock physician), keeps record and clock, shows the guideline read as a card. AI-guided opt-in. Demo P added.

Always design for the user. The AI agent is a tool that connects doctors; these tools connect people, not the AI. Connector with intelligence: is it a STEMI, the accepting physician, the time, lytics are here, and if things fail we go here. All projects geared for New Mexico rural health.
Connector card built: five things on both screens; guideline read behind a tap. Design law written into both skills; ER physician panel added to the roster.
Allow an accelerated pathway: frustrated doctors will just say 'connect me to the interventionalist'. It has to be very nimble.

The agent should be a scribe, not make recommendations; clinical decisions are for real doctors. EKG, STEMI, connect me to the interventionalist, boom. No AI narrative — that's for someone without the understanding.
Scribe is now the default model; Guided is opt-in; Express connects on the first words or one tap. ECG photo → one-line read → dial. 104/104 tests.

Multiple people in the chain: ER physician, charge nurses, house supervisor (beds), receiving ED physician. Who needs to know, what they need, roll out in stages: phones → three-way call → automation. Every condition needs its own team.
Add this as a skill; my development team will integrate it into our Systems Builder.

inventoryNotes: Written by the scribe run of 2026-09-12 from index.md, log.md and the first ~40 lines of each classified note. Caveats: (1) File mtimes are unreliable — a bulk Baalda resync stamped many notes 2026-09-12 11:14, so every lastTouched is taken from the note's own frontmatter/content date, not the filesystem. (2) log.md stops at 2026-09-09 while files dated 09-10 through 09-13 exist, so the log lags the vault by three to four days; ONE CALL, funding and governance activity after 09-09 is sourced from the notes themselves. (3) No ECMO book chapter exists anywhere in the vault or the saved listing — that item in the brief could not be confirmed and is not represented. (4) 2026-08-29_nmcsn-registry_irb-protocol-draft is listed in index.md but the file is not present in the vault; T39 covers that. (5) The 'documents' engine (E2) and 'process' engine (E3) already on the board absorb the strategy documents (master plan, board prospectus, backer brief, global roadmap, pitch decks, decision roadmap) and the factory/floor/systems-builder/Baalda work respectively — those files are deliberately not duplicated into new engines here, though several governance and funding items cross-reference them. (6) States are judged from dates and explicit status lines; where a note carried no status the state is inferred from the latest dated activity and should be treated as provisional — this applies especially to education (backlog, nothing since May 2026), website (backlog, nothing since 08-30) and the AMICS transfer paper milestone (backlog, nothing since 08-16). (7) Missoula is marked done because the talk was delivered 2026-08-24 and the projects index carrying it was archived, but whether the relationship continues is an open Ray decision (T109). (8) Owner assignments are suggestions mapped from each item's nature onto the roster; only items that the record itself says require Ray are given owner 'ray'.
